key_insight: Share learns a compact, shared low-rank LoRA subspace that new-task updates project into and occasionally consolidate into, enabling near-zero forgetting continual adaptation of large pretrained models without data replay or growing per-task adapters.
problem_solved: Efficient continual adaptation of large pretrained models while avoiding catastrophic forgetting, replay buffers, and the memory/compute bloat of separate adapters per task.
method: Maintain a small shared low-rank LoRA subspace for parameter-efficient updates; represent new-task updates as coefficients in that subspace instead of independent adapters.

When necessary, expand or consolidate the shared subspace by integrating important task directions (with orthogonality/regularization constraints) so knowledge is merged rather than kept in separate modules.
Train/update only the low-rank coefficients (and occasional compact basis updates), enabling almost strict continual learning without replay and with bounded memory/computation.
impact: Practitioners can continually adapt large models on-device or in constrained infra with much lower memory and compute, reducing deployment complexity (single adapter) while preserving prior task performance—critical for real-world, multi-task systems.

paper_title: Shared LoRA Subspaces for almost Strict Continual Learning
paper_authors: Prakhar Kaushik, Ankit Vaidya, Shravan Chaudhari, Rama Chellappa, Alan Yuille
